_comment: Objects that `make download` fetched but no package claims through its
Source: field. They arrive through custom Download rules, which OpenWrt
registers unconditionally, so the download set is not the same as the set
the boards build.
Whether such an object belongs in a published source-cache cannot be
derived: usb-modeswitch-data is needed by a package we select, and the
Broadcom firmware is needed by nothing we select. Both look identical to a
script -- fetched, unattributed -- so the difference is written down here
rather than guessed at publish time.
decision:
include  goes into source-cache/. Something we build needs it.
exclude  withheld. Nothing we build needs it, and shipping a file we do
not need is a redistribution question we have no reason to open.
make-downloads-lock.sh refuses to run while an unattributed object has no
entry here. A new one appearing is a change in what the build pulls, and
that should stop a release rather than ride along in it.
patches/common/base-files/002-mac80211-download-broadcom-fw-only-when-selected.patch
now guards both Broadcom Download rules on their config symbols, so a fresh
collection no longer fetches them at all: 166 objects instead of 168, verified.
The two entries below are kept as the record of why. If that patch is ever
dropped the files come back, and the decision that covers them is already here.

objects.reason: Broadcom proprietary wireless firmware. No CONFIG_PACKAGE_kmod-b43* is selected on any of the six boards, so nothing we build uses it; the download rule is registered unconditionally and fires regardless of configuration.
objects.evidence: grep -cE '^CONFIG_PACKAGE_(kmod-b43|kmod-brcmsmac)' on every board config returns 0

objects.reason: As above. Broadcom firmware for brcmsmac, unused by every board we ship.
objects.evidence: grep -cE '^CONFIG_PACKAGE_(kmod-b43|kmod-brcmsmac)' on every board config returns 0

objects.reason: The device database usbmode installs. CONFIG_PACKAGE_usb-modeswitch=y on the boards, so the package is built and this is its second source.
